newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Hellaby has Expozay, Hannahs options.
newsitem.headline: Hellaby has Expozay, Hannahs options.

text.p: Investment company Hellaby Holdings Ltd said it had an option to subscribe for 51 percent of footwear company R. Hannah and Co and 100 percent of Expozay International, a swimwear manufacturer.
Hannahs had engaged in an extensive restructuring during the past year, including the closure of a number of its unprofitable stores and the liquidation of its non-core property portfolio.
The company now sought to refurbish and build on its position.
Hellaby had agreed to provide NZ$5 million in subordinated secured debt to fund this programme and a further NZ$5.5 million to assist in restructuring existing banking arrangements.
Hellaby had also provided a loan guarantee of up to NZ$10 million, secured by a first ranking debenture.
In return, Hellaby received an option to subscribe for 51 percent of the shareholding in Hannahs, exercisable in 1997.

Expozay had suffered from the strength of the New Zealand dollar, the depressed apparel market and internal difficulties associated with moves to reduce the seasonality of its business. Hellaby intended exercising its option to acquire 100 percent of Expozay on January 1, 1997, at book value. The investment in Expozay, through advances and equity, would total NZ$3 million.
Expozay's existing management shareholders will be given share options to enable them to regain ownership of the company depending on its future performance, Hellaby said.
